title: Truncated higher-direct-image comparison
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a category small in a universe containing the sites and coefficients [def-weil-size-convention], endowed with two site structures $\tau$ and $\tau'$ [def-weil-pbc-sites-and-cohomology] such that every $\tau'$-covering is a $\tau$-covering. For $X\in\mathcal C$, let $\mathcal C_\tau/X$ and $\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X$ be the slice sites: their objects are arrows $U\to X$, their morphisms are commutative triangles, and their coverings are those whose underlying families cover $U$ in the respective topology. Let $\epsilon_X:\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)\to\mathrm{Sh}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ be the comparison geometric morphism [def-trf-geometric-morphism] with direct image the identity on underlying presheaves and inverse image $\tau$ sheafification [def-weil-pbc-sheafification]. For $f:X\to Y$ write $f_{\tau'}$ for the relocalization morphism of slice topoi whose inverse image sends $H$ to $(U\to X)\mapsto H(U\to X\to Y)$. Higher direct images below mean the ordinary right derived functors on abelian sheaves, computed using injective resolutions. Suppose that a class $\mathcal P$ of morphisms and full subcategories $\mathcal A'_X\subset\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_{\tau'}/X)$ have the following properties. Each $\mathcal A'_X$ contains zero and is closed under isomorphisms, kernels and cokernels of morphisms between its objects, and extensions (the weak Serre condition). Assume in addition:

(1) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$ and any $Y'\to Y$, the fibre product $X\times_Y Y'$ exists and $X\times_Y Y'\to Y'$ lies in $\mathcal P$.

(2) For every $f:X\to Y$, one has $f_{\tau'}^{-1}(\mathcal A'_Y)\subset\mathcal A'_X$.

(3) Every $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ already satisfies the $\tau$ sheaf condition on $\mathcal C/X$.

(4) For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$, $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$ and every $i\geq0$, one has $R^if_{\tau',*}H'\in\mathcal A'_Y$.

For each $X$, let $\mathcal A_X$ be the full subcategory of $\mathrm{Ab}(\mathcal C_\tau/X)$ consisting of sheaves isomorphic to $\epsilon_X^{-1}H'$ with $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$. For $r\geq0$, let $(V_r)$ mean that $R^i\epsilon_{X,*}H=0$ for all $X$, $H\in\mathcal A_X$ and $1\leq i\leq r$. Assume $(V_r)$. For $f:X\to Y$ in $\mathcal P$, $H\in\mathcal A_X$ and $0\leq i\leq r$, the canonical comparison is an isomorphism
$$R^if_{\tau',*}\epsilon_{X,*}H\xrightarrow{\sim}\epsilon_{Y,*}R^if_{\tau,*}H.$$
Here “canonical” specifies the following maps, not just existence of an isomorphism of sheaves. In the bounded-below derived categories [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], the map
$$a_H:Rf_{\tau',*}\epsilon_{X,*}H\longrightarrow Rf_{\tau',*}R\epsilon_{X,*}H\xrightarrow{\sim}R\epsilon_{Y,*}Rf_{\tau,*}H$$
is induced by $\epsilon_{X,*}H\to R\epsilon_{X,*}H$ and composition of derived direct images in the commutative square of slice topoi. The degree-$i$ comparison above is $\mathcal H^i(a_H)$ followed by the relative Leray edge $\mathcal H^i(R\epsilon_{Y,*}Rf_{\tau,*}H)\to\epsilon_{Y,*}R^if_{\tau,*}H$, which is an isomorphism in this range. The adjoint comparison is $b_H:\epsilon_Y^{-1}Rf_{\tau',*}\epsilon_{X,*}H\to Rf_{\tau,*}H$.

source.place: Tag 0EZA, lemma-V-implies-C-general; naturality/canonical maps are those of its proof and section-compare-general.

proof.text: Write $S_Z=\epsilon_Z^{-1}$ and $J_Z=\epsilon_{Z,*}$. Since $J_Z$ changes no underlying presheaf, it is fully faithful, and $S_ZJ_ZG=G$ for every $\tau$-sheaf $G$: sheafification fixes a sheaf by its universal property. If $H\cong S_XH'$ with $H'\in\mathcal A'_X$, assumption (3) gives $J_XH\cong H'\in\mathcal A'_X$. The functor $S_Z$ is exact: it is abelian sheafification restricted to $\tau'$-sheaves; kernels of sheaves are sectionwise and colimits are sheafified presheaf colimits. Thus the exactness statement for presheaf sheafification gives exactness also on this restricted domain.

source.place: section-compare, assertions (1)-(2); Tag 0EZA, preliminary identification of the coefficient class.

proof.text: Apply localization of a site morphism to the identity functor from the coarse slice category over $Y$ to the fine slice category over $Y$, localized at the object $f:X\to Y$. Its localized morphism is $\epsilon_X$, and its two horizontal localization morphisms are $f_\tau$ and $f_{\tau'}$. The inverse-image composition isomorphism gives the square in the statement; taking right adjoints gives $f_{\tau',*}J_X\cong J_Yf_{\tau,*}$. All inverse images on abelian sheaves are exact: they preserve finite limits as geometric inverse images and finite colimits as left adjoints. Hence each direct image preserves injectives. The categories have enough injectives, and the derived composition theorem gives the canonical isomorphism $Rf_{\tau',*}RJ_X\cong RJ_YRf_{\tau,*}$. Here use constant integer ring sheaves, for which modules are exactly abelian sheaves with their unique integer action; restrict the composition theorem to bounded-below objects. Set $B^i=\mathcal H^i(RJ_YRf_{\tau,*}H)$. The morphism $a_H$ in the statement is obtained from the augmentation $J_XH\to RJ_XH$ and this very composition isomorphism.

source.place: section-compare-general, equation-commutative-epsilon; Tag 0EZA, first displayed derived identity; Tag 0D6E, lemma-derived-pushforward-composition.

proof.text: For the pair $(J_X,f_{\tau',*})$, the site specialization of the Grothendieck spectral sequence gives $T_2^{p,q}=R^pf_{\tau',*}(R^qJ_XH)\Rightarrow B^{p+q}$. The acyclicity condition holds because Step 2 shows that $J_X$ preserves injectives. By $(V_r)$, rows $1\leq q\leq r$ vanish. For total degree $i\leq r$, only $(i,0)$ can remain. Its outgoing differentials have negative second index; an incoming differential on page $s\geq2$ would start at $(i-s,s-1)$, which either has negative first index or has $1\leq s-1\leq r$ and is zero. Thus the abutment filtration has a single nonzero graded piece in degree $i$, and the bottom edge $R^if_{\tau',*}J_XH\to B^i$ is an isomorphism. This edge is $\mathcal H^i(a_H)$: the bottom edge derives the augmentation $J_XH\to RJ_XH$, followed by the canonical composition comparison, as in Step 2.

source.place: Tag 0EZA, passage from (V_n) to an isomorphism in degrees at most n, expressed using the Grothendieck bottom edge; Tag 0734, lemma-relative-Leray.

proof.text: Put $G_q=R^qf_{\tau,*}H$. The other composite $(f_{\tau,*},J_Y)$ gives a first-quadrant spectral sequence $E_2^{p,q}=R^pJ_YG_q\Rightarrow B^{p+q}$, with $d_s$ of bidegree $(s,1-s)$ and finite abutment filtrations. Its left edge is $e_q:B^q\to J_YG_q$. Its acyclicity condition again follows from preservation of injectives in Step 2. In degree zero there are no entering or leaving differentials and the filtration has only $(0,0)$. Consequently $e_0$ is invertible. Composing with Step 3 proves the specified comparison $c_0:R^0f_{\tau',*}J_XH\to J_YG_0$ is invertible. If $r=0$, this already proves every claimed degree.

source.place: Tag 0EZA, second-page diagram and base case (C_0); Tag 0734, lemma-relative-Leray.

proof.text: For $1\leq m\leq r$, suppose the specified comparisons $c_q$ have been proved invertible for $0\leq q<m$. By Step 1 and assumption (4), $R^qf_{\tau',*}J_XH$ belongs to $\mathcal A'_Y$. Therefore $J_YG_q$ belongs to $\mathcal A'_Y$ for $q<m$. The identity $S_YJ_YG_q=G_q$ then puts $G_q$ in $\mathcal A_Y$. Apply $(V_r)$ to these particular sheaves: $E_2^{p,q}=R^pJ_YG_q=0$ whenever $1\leq p\leq r$ and $0\leq q<m$. This uses only the already proved comparisons in strictly smaller degrees, so it sets up a genuine induction.

source.place: Tag 0EZA, calculation following (C_{m-1}); assumptions (3)-(4) in situation-compare.

proof.text: On the total-degree-$m$ diagonal, every term except $(0,m)$ has $1\leq p\leq m\leq r$ and $q<m$, so vanishes by Step 5. No differential enters $(0,m)$ in a first-quadrant sequence. A differential leaving it on page $2\leq s\leq m$ lands in $(s,m-s+1)$, also zero by Step 5. Pages $s>m+1$ have negative target second index. Only $d_{m+1}^{0,m}$ can remain, with target $E_{m+1}^{m+1,0}$, a subquotient of $R^{m+1}J_YG_0$. The filtration therefore identifies the left edge as a monomorphism $e_m:B^m\hookrightarrow J_YG_m$ with image the kernel of this last differential. If $m<r$, then $R^{m+1}J_YG_0=0$ by Step 5 and $(V_r)$, so $e_m$ is an isomorphism. With Step 3 this proves $c_m$ and continues the induction up to $m=r-1$.

source.place: Tag 0EZA, differential and filtration analysis for m<n, and the beginning of the final-degree analysis.

proof.text: For the remaining case $m=r\geq1$, the target of the possibly nonzero differential is exactly $R^{r+1}J_YG_0$. Indeed, before page $r+1$, outgoing differentials from $(r+1,0)$ have negative second index, while incoming ones have source $(r+1-s,s-1)$ with $1\leq r+1-s\leq r-1$ and $s-1<r$, so those sources vanish by Step 5. Thus $E_{r+1}^{r+1,0}=E_2^{r+1,0}$. Combining the kernel description in Step 6 with the isomorphism in Step 3 gives an exact sequence $0\to A\xrightarrow{c_r}J_YG_r\to R^{r+1}J_YG_0$, where $A=R^rf_{\tau',*}J_XH$. There is no assertion that the last differential vanishes before sheafification.

source.place: Tag 0EZA, final paragraph and its displayed exact sequence.

proof.text: Choose an injective resolution $G_0\to I^\bullet$ on the fine slice site. Then $R^{r+1}J_YG_0=H^{r+1}(J_YI^\bullet)$. Exactness of $S_Y$ and its compatibility with cohomology give $S_YR^{r+1}J_YG_0=H^{r+1}(S_YJ_YI^\bullet)=H^{r+1}(I^\bullet)=0$, since $r+1>0$. This is the source's sheafification-zero assertion, computed directly on the same injective resolution rather than quoting local vanishing as an extra lemma. Assumption (4) puts $A$ in $\mathcal A'_Y$, so assumption (3) says that $A$ is already a fine sheaf. The middle term $J_YG_r$ also is a fine sheaf, by definition. Apply exact $S_Y$ to Step 7: it makes $S_Y(c_r)$ invertible. Sheafification fixes both its source and target and their morphism, so $c_r$ itself is invertible. This completes the induction.

source.place: Tag 0EZA, last paragraph; section-compare, explanation Ad (3), the same injective-complex calculation for the derived counit.

proof.text: At every degree the map proved invertible was $c_i=e_i\circ\mathcal H^i(a_H)$. Step 3 proves the first factor from $a_H$ invertible, and Steps 4-8 prove the relative Leray edge $e_i$ invertible, for $0\leq i\leq r$. Thus the conclusion is about precisely the canonical maps prescribed in the statement. Under the derived adjunction $S_Y\dashv RJ_Y$, the adjoint of $a_H$ is $b_H$; explicitly it is $S_YRf_{\tau',*}J_XH\xrightarrow{S_Ya_H}S_YRJ_YRf_{\tau,*}H\to Rf_{\tau,*}H$ with the derived counit as last map. All comparisons used above are natural in the coefficient, being augmentations, composition comparisons and the two spectral-sequence edges.
